title: Meet P, Q and R
goal: Recognise, name and write P, Q, R.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
task: Point to P and R. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter P has a big form and a small form.
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 5 before looking back.

cards.title: Letter P
sections: In pen, p represents /p/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.

articulation.label: Letter P
articulation.alt: Letter P: /p/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter Q
sections: In queen, q and u work together as /kw/.
Write Q and q three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

cards.introduction: Learn this letter’s name. Look, listen, and write it.

articulation.label: Letter Q
articulation.alt: Letter Q: /k/ → /j/ → /u/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/j/: Front tongue high; glide into the next vowel.
/u/: High back tongue; round the lips.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.alt: Letter R: /ɑ/ → /r/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: something you write with. Write your name with this pen.
a female royal ruler. The queen wears a gold crown.
A small animal with long ears. The rabbit eats a leaf.
A farm animal with a round nose and short legs. The pig is on the farm.
water that falls from clouds. There is no rain today.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
